correctness.rationale: The exact coordinate update U_i=I-e_i(e_i^T H_rho) has unit coordinate curvature; invariant initial data and Hessian reduce 27 sequences to the four equality-pattern classes. All 27 terminal objective polynomials independently coincide with the formulas derived by direct substitution. The three exact difference factorizations prove the sign and sharp rho=1/2 boundary throughout -1/2<rho<1, while a 3:12:6:6 weighted sum gives the mean and its unique rho=4/5 root. Two-dimensional direct formulas prove minimality within this family. The SymPy verifier is reproduced from artifacts/verify.py, its output is included; finite samples are not substituted for the all-parameter factorization proof.

originality.rationale: The new assessed statement is the precise first-epoch distribution and its stochastic-order and 2/9 pathwise reversal, not the known setup or generic expected-objective comparison. Full accessible research passages in Lee–Wright (2016) and Gürbüzbalaban et al. (2018) concern expected contraction or structured convergent families, not the four-atom law. The 2022 SDP work estimates worst-case performance rather than giving this sampling-distribution classification. The 2025 related manuscript is only abstract-inspected, so a specialist priority risk is explicitly retained; abstract rate bounds do not logically imply realized loss probabilities. The public prior-result searches returned adjacent, non-dominating coordinate-sampling and Gauss–Seidel claims and no claim of this distribution. Absence of a search hit is not proof of priority.
residual_risks: Specialist publications not indexed in accessible searches may derive or explicitly tabulate the same 27 path outcomes.
The closely relevant 2025 manuscript was only available at abstract level; its appendices or examples may contain a more direct comparison not verified here.

value.rationale: A natural question in randomized numerical optimization is whether swapping coordinate sampling with replacement for random permutation improves every realized fixed-budget epoch, or merely the expected convergence rate. This complete minimal three-variable symmetric example separates those claims through a sharp 1/2 pathwise frontier, a nonzero fixed 2/9 probability of a better repeated-index outcome, and a distinct mean 4/5 frontier. The classification explains the underlying alternating revisit and supplies a reproducible exact test problem; it has a clear mathematical use beyond mere parameter substitution or a tiny empirical gain. No downstream theorem is asserted.
